chapter: Tatum, Wiggins and Los Angeles friends
title: Eddie Beal, Bumps Myers and the shared apartments
summary: Callender recalls being taken in by Bumps Myers's family and renting with Eddie Beal, and Willard recalls jam sessions at Beal's apartment.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Mentioning Eddie Beal: When I first came to California, Eddie Beal and Bumps Myers were like... They took me in like a long-lost brother. Bumps Myers, whose mother reminded me

so much of my mother, took me into their home, and treated me just like a second son. After that, my first meeting with Eddie Beal, we rented an apartment together, we rented an apartment together. This was way back in the very late Thirties. So we rented this apartment, and two weeks later Eddie Beal got married and moved out, so he never stayed there. Eddie Beal is one of my favorite characters, incidentally.

Yeah, mine too. Well, at that apartment... I met Eddie in 1948 or 1949 when he had an apartment on Montclair with Marian Sampler and Cal Bailey, (Marian Sampler, the fine artist, and Cal Bailey was also an artist), and was there anybody else... I guess it was the three of them who had that apartment.
It was the three of them.
And more music took place there...
And I think Nadine Cole owned that apartment.
But I remember being invited over there to jam sessions. Gerald Wiggins was always there...
And I think that the first place I ever heard Jimmy Jones play was at Eddie Beal's apartment.
